en: The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Great Master of the Dharma and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
under Imperial Decree during the Western Heavens Translation Era.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a vast assembly of bhikṣus and ten koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who possessed the marks of a youth.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas: "Kauśika!
This Prajñāpāramitā is of exceedingly profound meaning."

It is neither one nor different; neither with marks nor without marks; neither grasping nor relinquishing; neither increasing nor decreasing; neither possessing afflictions nor being free from afflictions; neither abandoning nor not abandoning; neither abiding nor not abiding; neither associated nor dissociated; neither affliction nor non-affliction; neither a condition nor a non-condition; neither real nor unreal; neither dharma nor non-dharma; neither having a place of refuge nor having no place of refuge; neither the limit of reality nor not the limit of reality.
“Kauśika! Just as all dharmas are equal, so too is the prajñāpāramitā equal;
just as all dharmas are quiescent, so too is the prajñāpāramitā quiescent.”
All phenomena are immovable, and the perfection of wisdom is also immovable;
all phenomena are differentiated, and the perfection of wisdom is also differentiated;
all phenomena are fearful, and the perfection of wisdom is also fearful.
All dharmas are fully known, and the Prajñāpāramitā is also fully known;
all dharmas are of one taste, and the Prajñāpāramitā is also of one taste;
all dharmas are unarisen, and the Prajñāpāramitā is also unarisen.
All dharmas are non-extinguished, and the prajñāpāramitā is also non-extinguished;
all dharmas are empty and conceptualized, and the prajñāpāramitā is also empty and conceptualized.
Form is boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless;
likewise, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
The earth element is boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless;
likewise, the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are boundless, and the perfection of wisdom is also boundless.
The vajra is equal, and the prajñāpāramitā is also equal.
All dharmas are indestructible, and the prajñāpāramitā is also indestructible;
the nature of all dharmas is unattainable, and the prajñāpāramitā is also unattainable.
The nature of all phenomena is equal, and the perfection of wisdom is also equal;
all phenomena are without intrinsic nature, and the perfection of wisdom is also without intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are inconceivable, and the perfection of wisdom is also inconceivable.

In this way, the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of skillful means, the perfection of aspiration, the perfection of power, and the perfection of wisdom are also inconceivable.
When the three karmas are pure, the *prajñāpāramitā* is also pure.
Such is the *prajñāpāramitā*; its meaning is boundless. "Furthermore, Kauśika!
There are all eighteen kinds of emptiness. What are the eighteen? They are:

internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, limitless emptiness, non-alteration emptiness, beginningless emptiness, essential nature emptiness, self-characteristic emptiness, signlessness emptiness, non-existence emptiness, self-nature emptiness, non-existence-of-self-nature emptiness, and the emptiness of all phenomena.
The verse says:
"Like stars, like lamps, and like a visual impairment; like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, and a dewdrop;
like lightning and also like clouds—one should contemplate them in this way."
I shall now briefly explain this Prajñāpāramitā:
it is neither arising nor ceasing, neither interrupted nor eternal;
its meaning is neither one nor many, and it neither comes nor goes.
Thus, the Perfectly Awakened One has taught that these twelve links of dependent origination are brought to cessation and stilled.
I take refuge in the Buddhas of the ten directions— those of the past, present, and future.
The Perfection of the Three Jewels.
An ocean of immeasurable merit, making offerings to all Tathāgatas—this is the great illumination of true secrecy.
The mantra says:
Tadyathā | prajñe prajñe mahāprajñe prajñāvabhāse |
*Praruṅkā-kārya-ajñāna-vighnani-siddhi-susiddhi*
Siddhyaṃ dūṃ svāhā sarvāgāsunnarivartte vaśre.
praśritahastisamāsakaṭiṣvaṣvaṣvaṣvaṣvaṣvaḥ
Khaṃba khaṃba, vāma vāma, rava rava.
āgaccha āgaccha bhagavati mām avala svāhā. Namo dārimudrāgatāya bodhisattvāya.
Mahāsattva, Mahākāruṇika, namo sanāprarudite, bodhisattva.
Mahāsattva, Mahākāruṇika, namo ’pratihatajñānaprāptāye. Tadyathā: muñce darime.
Saṃgrahatāre ’nugrahatāre vimuktatāre sattvānugrahatāre.
Vaiśravaṇadarimi samantanuparivartanadarimi yugandhara-ha-saṃgara-ha-darimi sarvatrānugata-darimi.
Sarvakālaparipūrṇapraṇidhim svāhā prajñāpāramitāyāḥ.
Recite: *tadyathā akhani akhani akhanani khani avāra-vandani bhañjani bhañjani praṇasvāhā*. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai.
Oṃ āgā āgā nate āgā nate navaśāgā svāhā. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai. Tadyathā: śriye śriye.
Maṇiśriye maṇiśriya-svāhā.
prajñāpāramitāye tadyathā oṃ.
Vajrāvele svāhā. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai tadyathā...
Hūṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śruti-tiṣṭha-samitigati-vijaya svāhā. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai. Tadyathā: vaṃ varivaṃ mahāvaṃ dharu dharu mahā...
Dhuru svāhā. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai tadyathā | hūte hūte hūtase sarvakalpa-varaṇe svāhā. Namo prajñāpāramitāyai tadyathā...
Join them with: Oṃ aruke svāhā. “Namo prajñāpāramitāyai tadyathā oṃ sarvavidu svāhā. “Namo prajñāpāramitāyai tadyathā gate gate pāra-”

"Oṃ rāgadveṣamoha svāhā. At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra, Śakra Devendra, the various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, devas, humans, gandharvas, asuras, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom Spoken by the Buddha for Śakra Devānām Indra.
